content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day window, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after sharp price increases, then corrects downward — suggesting lag in adjusting to recent volatility.
- Mean reversion is overestimated: model assumes prices quickly return to historical averages, but true outcomes show slower reversion with persistent downward drift.
- Forecasts are too conservative in the final 5–10 days of the 30-day window, underestimating downward momentum.
- Model exhibits bias toward lower values when recent history includes high prices — fails to capture “highs are not necessarily followed by lows” in short-term context.
- Over-reliance on recent 7–14 day averages leads to underestimating price drops after spikes.
- Forecasting horizon of 30 days shows persistent lag — true prices often dip below forecast by day 10–15, suggesting model doesn’t adjust to new information quickly enough.
